title: The bootstrap
summary: Bootstrapping re-estimates the model on many resamples of the data to show how much an estimate would vary from sample to sample.

body.text: PLS-SEM makes no distributional assumption from which standard errors could be derived, so it uses the [[bootstrap]] (Efron & Tibshirani 1993): draw B samples of the same size n from your data with replacement, re-estimate the model on each, and look at the distribution of the B estimates.

body.caption: Resample a small fixed sample. The spread of the resampled estimates approximates sampling variability; the same seed gives the same draws.

body.text: The [[standard-error]] is the standard deviation of the bootstrap estimates, and percentile confidence intervals are read off their quantiles (next lesson). Because the draws are random, results depend slightly on B and on the [[random-seed]]. SEM Studio requires a seed so that every result can be reproduced exactly, and the exported R and Python scripts draw the same resamples.

Use a few hundred draws to explore and several thousand for reported results; if a conclusion changes when you rerun with another seed, B is too small or the effect is borderline. Report B, the seed and the interval type (Streukens & Leroi-Werelds 2016).

mistake.title: Changing the seed until p < .05
mistake.text: Rerunning with different seeds and keeping the "best" result is p-hacking. Fix the seed and B before running, and report them.

tryIt.task: Open the TAM example; its analysis settings already request 5,000 bootstrap draws with a fixed seed. Run it and inspect the bootstrap distribution of PEOU → BI on the Results page.

checks.question: What does the bootstrap standard error of a path represent?

options.text: The standard deviation of the path across the bootstrap resamples, an estimate of its sampling variability.
The standard deviation of the indicators.
options.feedback: Indicator SDs describe the data, not the uncertainty of an estimate.

options.text: The average error of the model's predictions.
options.feedback: Prediction error is a different concept; the SE concerns the estimate of a parameter.

checks.explanation: SE = spread of an estimate across samples.

checks.question: You rerun a bootstrap with a different seed and the confidence limits change in the third decimal. What does that mean?

options.text: Monte Carlo variation from a finite number of draws; more draws reduce it.
options.feedback: Correct. It is expected and should not change conclusions if B is large enough.
Small differences between seeds come from random resampling, not from the model.

options.text: The first result was wrong and the second is right.
options.feedback: Both are valid approximations of the same bootstrap distribution.
